name: Meridian Munitions Viper PDW MVP-3 'Sidewinder'
description:
The MVP-3 Sidewinder is Meridian Munitions' compact personal defense weapon, designed for operators who need maximum firepower in minimum space. The weapon uses a telescoping bolt design that wraps around the barrel, reducing overall length to 280mm with the stock folded while maintaining a 180mm barrel for adequate velocity. Chambered in 5.7mm caseless armor-piercing, the Sidewinder punches above its weight class against body armor.

The BCI aim-assist module is the same open-architecture system used in the MM-4 Breadwinner, maintaining Meridian's commitment to non-proprietary accessories. A rail-mounted micro red dot is included as standard, and the weapon accepts any manufacturer's suppressor on its threaded barrel. The 25-round magazine fits flush with the grip, maintaining the compact profile.

At Φ2,200, the Sidewinder occupies the mid-range of the PDW market. It lacks the BCI sophistication of Tessera's Reflex and the rock-bottom pricing of Kang-Petrov's Rattler, but it delivers reliable performance with armor-piercing capability in a package that fits inside a laptop bag. For the freelancer who needs a concealable weapon that can defeat body armor, the MVP-3 is the practical choice.
specifications:
caliber: 5.7mm caseless AP
effective_range: 150m
rate_of_fire: 850 rpm (cyclic)
magazine_capacity: 25 rounds
weight: 1.6 kg
tactical_use: The Sidewinder provides armor-piercing capability in a concealable package. Its 5.7mm AP round defeats Level II body armor at close range and degrades Level III protection, giving operators a response to armored threats that pistol-caliber weapons cannot address. The compact dimensions allow concealed carry in civilian environments where a visible weapon would compromise the operation. The open-architecture BCI module means operators already using Meridian's ecosystem can transfer their settings directly.
cultural_context: The Sidewinder is the freelancer's insurance policy — the weapon carried when the job description says 'no weapons expected' but experience says otherwise. Its popularity among couriers, negotiators, and fixers reflects the reality that GLMZ's professional class moves through danger zones as part of their daily routine. The MVP-3 doesn't start fights. It finishes the ones that find you.
story_hooks: A courier's Sidewinder was the only weapon available when their convoy was ambushed. The 25-round magazine held off attackers long enough for extraction — barely.
Meridian is developing an upgraded Sidewinder with a 40-round extended magazine, but the prototype was stolen from their R&D facility along with the production blueprints.
related_entities: Vespid Dynamics Pheromone Marker Gun PMG-1 'Breadwinner'

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, angular submachine gun with an aggressive wedge-shaped profile. The telescoping bolt wrapped around the barrel creates a distinctive bulge along the top receiver. The folded stock configuration makes it appear almost as wide as it is long—a dense, efficient package rather than a traditional elongated PDW silhouette.
physical_description.dimensions: 280mm overall length (stock folded), 380mm extended; 180mm barrel; 65mm width at receiver; 130mm height with rail-mounted optic
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and surprisingly handy at 1.6kg—light enough for one-handed tactical transitions but substantial enough to manage 850 rpm recoil. The weight distribution favors the hand due to the compact barrel, making it feel controllable rather than whippy.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite frame with steel receiver barrel and internal bolt assembly. The polymer is industrial-grade to handle sustained fire without flex.
physical_description.finish: Matte black polymer with brushed steel receiver showing micro-serration marks from precision machining. The barrel wears a dark gray DLC (diamond-like carbon) coating for corrosion resistance.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary matte black with brushed steel accents on the receiver and bolt cover. Rail system in dark gunmetal gray. Accent striping in corporate steel blue along the mag well.
physical_description.grip_texture: Aggressively textured rubberized polymer with vertical grip ridges. The pistol grip wraps slightly forward—designed for off-hand stabilization in confined spaces. Magazine well features thumb-rest indexing.
distinctive_features: Telescoping bolt housing creating pronounced upper receiver bulge
Integrated rail-mounted Tier 2 micro red dot (factory standard)
BCI module interface panel on left receiver side—exposed connector port
Ambidextrous fire selector with detent positions clearly marked
Heat vent slots running along the upper polymer shroud
Charging handle integrated into the bolt telescope—recessed flush when forward
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: MERIDIAN MUNITIONS logo stamped in brushed relief on the left receiver. Serial plate mounted on the magwell with small Φ symbol indicating currency tier. MVP-3 designation lasered on the dust cover. Made in GLMZ barcode on the grip tang.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-ready and well-maintained. Light operational wear on grip texture from gloved handling, minor scope shadow on the receiver from optic mounting. No battle scars—the Sidewinder is a working tool kept in combat-ready condition by professionals.
